name: hazel_weir_central_procedural_graph
description: Optimized Central Procedural Graph with corrected land expansion triggers, deferred worker drop-offs for step efficiency, and tightened liquidation thresholds to preserve order slots.

nodes.name: State & Balance Audit
nodes.description: Computes net available cash, shed fill percentage, wage liability, active shop contract demand, and oracle price drop signals across market commodities.

nodes.name: Midnight Wage Reserve Defense
nodes.description: Protects payroll for all active hired hands. Enforces dynamic cash reserve locks and triggers pre-midnight surplus liquidation to prevent the 0-hand bankruptcy cascade.

nodes.name: Town Shop Demand Arbitrage
nodes.description: Preemptively matches unlocked town shop demand surges and immediately fulfills mature high-margin crops (Carrots, Tomatoes, Pumpkins, Strawberries) to capture 2.0x-3.5x contract price premiums.

nodes.name: Shed Headroom Relief
nodes.description: Prevents silent 100/100 harvest discards by clearing uncommitted low-margin inventory under strict price floors while protecting animal feed and shop contracts.

nodes.name: Oracle Opponent Front-Run
nodes.description: Reads 96-step TTM forecast to dump sensitive commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) immediately before opponent market gluts collapse prices.

nodes.name: Capital Reinvestment & Yield Scaling
nodes.description: Reinvests surplus cash beyond wage reserves into workforce acceleration (10-hand rush), contiguous land expansion, commercial high-yield seeds, and fertilizer.

nodes.name: Routine Farm & Workforce Execution
nodes.description: Executes field routines with strict operational sequencing: harvest ready crops, watering, planting, livestock feeding, and ground maintenance, optimizing drop-offs.

attributes.guidance: Cancel non-essential purchases (BUY_SEED, BUY_ANIMAL, BUY_LAND, redundant HIRE); schedule worker harvest drop-offs before hour 22; enforce emergency liquidation of non-feed, non-contract inventory at hour >= 20 to guarantee payroll.
attributes.pitfalls: Never sell Wheat below dynamic livestock feed reserve (max(4, n_animals * 3)); do not rely on low-margin fertilizer sales to cover payroll deficits; never liquidate crops committed to active town shop delivery.

attributes.guidance: Allocate up to 3 market slots to deliver matching mature shed inventory directly to town shops for 2.0x-3.5x premium; procure shop-demanded seeds (Carrots, Tomatoes, Pumpkins) when surplus cash covers seed costs and wage buffers.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not commit seed capital if net cash falls below 1.25x midnight payroll reserve; do not purchase shop seeds if shed capacity exceeds 88%; never hold shop produce past contract expiration windows.

attributes.guidance: Evict pending non-urgent buy orders to free order slots; execute batch sales of unreserved, non-shop surplus holdings with price >= 0.75 * base_price; only relax floor to 0.50 * base_price if shed_used >= 95 to prevent discard drops.
attributes.pitfalls: Never fire-sell at sub-0.50 base price during transient shed spikes; never liquidate Wheat below livestock feed reserve (max(4, n_animals * 3)); never evict produce allocated for active town shop fulfillment.

attributes.guidance: Preempt lowest-margin open orders; execute rapid batch liquidations of vulnerable commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) while current market price remains favorable (> 0.85 * base_price) before opponent dumping collapses market prices.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not dump into already collapsed sub-0.50 base price markets unless shed overflow is imminent; do not front-run commodities committed to active town shop contracts.

attributes.guidance: Aggressively scale workforce to the 10-hand cap by early-to-mid game; purchase contiguous land plots whenever uncultivated plots <= 2 to expand cultivation acreage; procure high-margin commercial seeds (Pumpkins, Tomatoes, Strawberries) and fertilizer to maximize per-plot harvest throughput.
attributes.pitfalls: Never allocate reinvestment capital if net cash after purchase drops below 1.25x midnight wage buffer; do not acquire land plots that hands cannot consistently water; halt land/hand capital expansion after day 27 to maximize terminal cash accumulation.

attributes.guidance: Dispatch active hands strictly by operational priority: 1) Harvest mature crops; 2) Water dry crops; 3) Plant commercial seeds; 4) Feed hungry livestock; 5) Weed clearing and ground tilling; 6) Drop off carried items at shed only when inventory is full or at end of day. Ensure all carried inventory is deposited at shed by step 716 for terminal liquidation.
attributes.pitfalls: Never prioritize weeding over harvesting or watering; do not leave mature crops unharvested across multi-step windows; ensure hands never idle while unharvested crops or dry plots remain; avoid premature drop-offs that waste walking steps.
